children: The Federal Trade Commission said Beretta Holding and Sturm, Ruger
agreed to accept a proposed consent order that prevents anticompetitive "entanglements" between two of the largest firearm makers.
Under the terms of the proposed consent order, Beretta, a subsidiary of Upifra, will be prohibited from appointing or nominating anyone to serve on Ruger's
board unless that person is independent of Beretta, according to an FTC statement on Wednesday.

for the company's board, arguing that years of weak performance and poor capital allocation require new oversight.

The consent agreement settles allegations that Beretta and Ruger's proposed stock purchase deal would create an “illegal interlocking” directorate arrangement in violation of Section 8 of the Clayton Act, which usually prohibits directors  and officers from serving simultaneously on the boards of competitors.

“Competition thrives best when the temptation to collude and share sensitive information isn’t on the table,” said Taylor C. Hoogendoorn, Deputy Director of the FTC’s Bureau of Competition, in a statement on Wednesday. “Competition between gunmakers helps ensure that Americans can exercise their Second Amendment rights. The FTC’s order aims to preserve the independence of a significant American gunmaker and removes the risk of anticompetitive coordination between two of the largest firearm manufacturers by taking decisive action to prevent anticompetitive interlocking directorates from forming."
The commission voted to issue the complaint and accept the consent agreement for public comment 2-0.
